intro: You are at Arslanhane Mosque, below Ankara castle in Ankara province, built in 1290. Step into a forest of wooden columns: this is a wooden hypostyle mosque, and its stucco mihrab is among the most elaborate pieces of Seljuk plasterwork.
history: The mosque below Ankara castle was built around 1290, and it takes its name from the Roman lion relief set into its wall. Its wooden hypostyle plan is joined to a stucco mihrab that is among the most elaborate pieces of Seljuk plasterwork. Beside it stands the tomb of Ahi Şerafeddin.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the stucco mihrab and the wooden columns, then the walnut minbar and the tomb of Ahi Şerafeddin.
facts: Did you know? The mosque was the Ankara seat of the Ahi brotherhood, and the craft guilds held their meetings here. And its name comes from the Roman lion relief set into its wall.
outro: This brings our visit to Arslanhane Mosque to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave everything untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. This wood and plaster have lasted for centuries; let them last for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
